rationale: B wins because it is more honest about what is blocked before a founder walks into a reporter's inbox. Its line, "No outside news signal was supplied, so the announcement itself is the only clock," is the right discipline; A's "Only a company with no shareholders to please could give repairs away" turns a useful ownership question into a thesis the supplied facts do not prove. Both sets have real material, but B does a better job separating story from wishful framing.
gaps_in_A: "Only a company with no shareholders to please could give repairs away" overclaims the ownership fact. The update says privately held and profits directed to environmental causes; it does not prove "only" or "no shareholders to please."
"triages it into free/at-cost/resale" invents an operational link between repair intake and the resale platform. The update says both exist, not that repair items get routed into resale.

"The announcement notably contains no new apparel line" is treated as strategic evidence without the necessary caveat. No line was announced here; that is not the same as Patagonia having no product push.
"four viable shapes exist" is too sunny. The data angle needs the 500,000 timeframe, and the operations angle needs basic mechanics before either is cleanly pitchable.
gaps_in_B: "Patagonia puts a repair counter in every US store" invents a physical counter and likely in-store repair function. The facts only support drop-off at stores plus mail-in.
"Patagonia's newest store rollout has nothing new to sell" overreads "no new apparel line announced." B catches the caveat later, but the headline still sells the overclaim.

"store labor, service counters, and what retailers do with floor space beyond selling" depends on the same unproven in-store-counter assumption. If stores are just intake points, that angle shrinks fast.

"The last item is required for this story type" is too rigid for the service angle. A price list, shipping policy, and turnaround time could support a useful consumer-service piece without a customer anecdote.
